CORE_MECHANISM_RESOLVED_2026-08-03.death_respawn_always_uses_the_safe_ancho: FUNC_8005B134 (respawn_transition_state_handler, states v0 in [3,10]) has a common tail at 0x8005b1bc..0x8005b2dc that unconditionally reads the safe anchor (0x800A6550/54/58) and writes it into the live position (0x800A6500/04/08) and the previous/render copy (0x800A6510/14/18), then zeroes a large block of player state (velocity/flags/counters). The scene spawn table (FUNC_80046B20 via FUNC_8005B714, 0x80077314+scene_id*12) is used ONLY at level entry, never as a fallback for death respawn -- there is no 'fallback spawn-table selection' path for death; the anchor governs unconditionally. Source: archived provenance ObsidianVault/Archive/Superseded/Functions_FUNC_8005B134.md (cross-checked against the current thin Canon page, consistent).

ANSWER_TO_OPERATOR_QUESTION: Yes, banked now (was not previously). In Cliffside Canyon specifically, death respawn IS a pre-determined location -- but not because death respawn generally uses a fixed table (it doesn't; the general rule is a continuously-tracked 'last safe position' anchor). Cliffside is a documented special case: its own scene_id (6) is hard-excluded from the anchor's continuous update, and the bird hazard's own overlay code writes a hardcoded literal coordinate into the anchor at the exact moment of death, distinct from both the scene's entry point and wherever Flik actually was.
